questions.question: PR #1159 is open. Should I watch it for CI results and review comments?
Agreed: today the Dafny file proves the model, the tests sample the code, and nothing ties the two together. Which validation do you want built for BE-033?

options.label: Model as oracle + mutation (Recommended)
options.description: Compile KernelProtocol.dfy to Python, as MemoryBackend.dfy already is. The kernel's real exits are then checked against the proved model, exhaustively over the whole finite space (routes, exits, runtimes, closable, posture) instead of by sampling. Then run the repo's mutation tooling (pytest-gremlins via run_mutate) on the protocol code to measure which code changes the tests actually catch. This ties model and code together and measures test strength. It adds one compiled oracle and a CI step; about M effort.

options.label: Exhaustive enumeration only
options.description: Replace the Hypothesis sampling with a generated suite over the full finite exit space, as test_condition_space.py does for other clauses. Every combination runs every time, and no Dafny build is involved. Stronger than sampling, but the model and the code are still not linked. About S effort.

options.label: TLA+ for close/run races
options.description: Model concurrent close against in-flight calls in sdd/formal/tla/ and run the TLC model checker on it. This is the only option that covers concurrency, which neither the tests nor Dafny touch. But the race belongs to the Session, which doesn't exist yet, so this is BK-455's scope. About M effort, and it delays this PR.

options.label: Keep PR, file item
options.description: Leave this PR as it is and file a backlog item for linking model and code. It records the gap, and the PR stays smaller.

How far should mutation testing go in this PR?

options.label: kernel.py + weekly scope (Recommended)
options.description: Mutation-test the async kernel.py now and kill any protocol survivors with new cells. Also add a kernel scope to scripts/mutate_scopes.py so the weekly mutation CI keeps covering src/remote_store/_kernel/. A local run takes about 15 minutes or more.

options.label: kernel.py only
options.description: Mutate kernel.py now and fix the survivors. Don't change the weekly CI scope, so the PR stays smaller.

options.label: Weekly scope only
options.description: Add only the CI scope, and leave the kernel.py findings to the first weekly run as a follow-up.

options.label: Stop here
options.description: Record the current results (_io.py 20/20, 45/62 overall) in the trace, and go on to /ship round 3.
